To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

S-100 protein positive sustentacular and S-100 positive Schwann like cells are present in embryonic and early fetal human sympathetic ganglia and that the sustentacular and the Schwann like cells have a different origin.

the sympathetic neuroblast clusters in human embryos are surrounded by a Schwann cell-derived basement membrane and are in contact with sustentacular cells, which probably develop from Schwann-like cells.

S-100 protein positive Schwann-like cells and sustentacular cells surround sympathetic neuroblasts during their migration in human embryos and fetal adrenal glands, suggesting the extra-adrenal origins of the sustentacu lar cells in the embryonic and fetal adrenals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin and development of the sustentacula in sympathetic ganglia and adrenal glands, and with their possible role in the development of sympathetic neuroblastic tumours.
the origin, distribution and differentiation of sustentacular cells and Schwann-like (or Schwann) cells in the sympathetic neuroblastic chain.
the origin and development of the sustentacu-lar cells in the sympathetic neuroblastic chain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
S-100 protein is expressed in two distinct types of cells, Schwann-like and sustentacular, which surround the sympathetic neuroblast groups from the paravertbral region to the fetal adrenal glands.
S-100 protein is expressed by sustentacular and sustentacular precursor Schwann-like cells in embryonic sympathetic neuroblasts as well as in the adrenal gland.
the Schwann-like cells and the sustentacular or the sustentacular precursor cell types are both present in human embryonic sympathetic neuroblasts at week 7 of gestation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sympathetic neuroblastic cells, their sustentacular cells and the Schwann-like cells are all present at 7 weeks gestation, and that the adrenal glands are invaded and penetrated by these cells at the same time.

the S-100 protein immunohistochemistry in combination with the staining for type IV collagen is a useful method for identifying the Schwann-like and the sustentacular precursor cell populations in human fetal sympathetic neuroblastoma.
S-100 protein is present in sustentacular cells and Schwann-like cell in human fetal sympathetic neuroblats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the S-100 protein is a marker of Schwann-like cells and of sustentacular cells.
the S100 protein is a marker for Schwann cells, and the S100 protein can be used to identify these cells.
